description: Antigravity CLI (agy) 1.5.9 sanitized MCP configuration sample (~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json), desensitized from the remote evidence run on Debian 13 (docs/verification/remote-workflow/agy-1.5.9/). Key contract observed on 1.5.9: the native writer (agy mcp add) spells remote entries serverUrl and stamps an explicit disabled:false on every entry it writes; the builtin docs describe url as the current key with serverUrl accepted as legacy — both keys are read (agy mcp list recognizes either), and a native edit of a legacy url entry rewrites it back to serverUrl, never leaving both keys pointing at different addresses. agy mcp enable removes the disabled key entirely (implicit enabled). Unknown native fields (cwd, trust, ...) survive edits of other entries but a native re-add of the same entry rebuilds it from flags only.
